sentences.text: "Learned counsel for the applicants and learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 are present.
As parties are said to have been arrived at a compromise.
The dispute is matrimonial.
The compromise between the parties would not affect the society adversely.

As some of the sections involved are non-compoundable, hence this court is prayed to issue a direction to the trial court to verify the compromise deed of the parties so that the compromise deed may be placed before the Court for its acceptance.

As parties are said to have been arrived at a compromise and certified copy of the compromise deed is appended at page 11 of the counter affidavit, hence, the parties are directed to appear before the trial court within 15 days from today along with their compromise deed.

If the parties appear before the trial court within the time stipulated, the trial court shall verify the said compromise deed, pass a verification order thereon and transmit a certified copy of the verified compromise deed along with the certified copy of the verification order passed thereon to this Court within 15 days thereafter.

Till the next date of listing, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant. "
4.

Pursuant to the order of this Court dated 27.04.2023, learned Civil Judge (J.D.)/ F.T.C.- 1, Agra has verified the compromise between the parties on 9.5.2023 and information to this effect has been received before this Court on 9.5.2023.

5. Ms. Simi Siddiqui, advocate holding brief of Sri Mazhar Ullah, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has not objected the aforesaid fact and submitted that in case proceedings is quashed, he would have no objection.
6. In view of above, the applicants and opposite party no. 2 do not want to pursue the case any further as stated by them.
The matter has been mutually settled between the parties, therefore, no useful purpose would be served in proceeding with the matter further.

7. Thus in view of the well settled principle of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the matters of Krishnappa & Ors. vs. State of Karnataka; 2021 0 Supreme(SC) 529, Parbatbhai Aahir @
Parbatbhai Bhimsinhbhai Karmur and Ors. vs. State of Gujarat and another; 2017 9 SCC 641, B.S.
Joshi Vs. State of Haryana; 2003(4) SCC 675, Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Burea of Investigation and another; (2008) 9 Supreme Court Cases 677, Gian Singh Vs. Stated of Punjab; (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab and another; (2014) Supreme Today 642, the proceedings of the aforesaid case is hereby quashed.
